header.name: Human Microbiome Data Science
header.description: The human microbiome has, in recent times, been increasingly regarded as an "organ", crucial for our well-being and healthspan. Advancements in DNA sequencing and experimental techniques, coupled with development of efficient data-analytic strategies using Statistical Learning (SL), Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML), have considerably expanded the purview and the resolution of human microbiome studies. \nThe course will cover the current state-of-the-art in human microbiome research along with the associated data analytic strategies. It will explore a range of topics covering the entire breadth of human microbiome research ranging from understanding the microbial ecology in different body sites to the strategies utilizing AI/ML/SL for designing microbiome targeted personalized diagnostics (Dx) and therapeutics (Tx). A key highlight will be discussions of actual published case studies that investigated the above aspects.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students should conceptually define the steps of the generation and pre-processing of microbiome data

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students should  describe and distinguish the variation in the properties of the human microbiome from different human body sites, design body-site-specific microbiome investigation and data-analysis studies using both novel data as well as large publicly available microbiome data

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students understand and summarise the relationship of the human microbiome with the different components/attributes of the host (like demographics, diet, medication, transcriptome, metabolome) and utilise this information to design microbiome-targeted personalised disease/treatment response prediction strategies.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students summarise, design and implement statistical and SL/ML-based data analytic protocols to different microbiome data sets (besides Bacterial/Archaeal/Protist metagenomic data sets) and perform different multi-OMIC investigations.

outcomes.label: CO5
outcomes.raw_text: Students list, describe, critique and justify various forms of AI and advanced-ML-based strategies utilised in Microbiome Research, along with examples and challenges for each

lecture_topics: Overview of the microbiome data generation approach from sequencing till the generation of taxonomy/function-based alpha and beta diversity profiles
Specific characteristics of the human microbiome at different body sites and its implications for the various data generation and analysis strategies
Large-scale publicly available human microbiome datasets (metagenomes + Metagenome-Assembled + Isolate genomes) along with host/isolation-source metadata
